verdict_json.summary: Raw_event shows certutil invoked via cmd.exe with -urlcache -split -f to fetch http://203.0.113.7/a.bin into C:\Users\Public\a.bin as E2EA\j.doe on HOST-A2, consistent with LOLBAS-documented download abuse in research. Correlations link the same host and user to an unresolved critical ransomware-like rename alert (~10 minutes later) already labeled MALICIOUS. Asset marks HOST-A2 as a high-criticality Finance Windows 11 workstation, elevating impact; identity shows two alerts for this user in seven days on one host.
verdict_json.root_cause: Hypothesis only: an attacker or compromised session for E2EA\j.doe used living-off-the-land certutil (parented by cmd.exe) to stage a remote payload on HOST-A2, potentially as a precursor to the correlated ransomware-like activity; the dossier also flags the alert as synthetic E2E, so treat operational impact as unconfirmed until validated.
recommended_actions: Escalate and contain HOST-A2 (network isolate) given high-criticality Finance asset and unresolved malicious correlation
Hunt for and quarantine C:\Users\Public\a.bin; capture hash, timestamps, and related process tree if present
Block or monitor 203.0.113.7 and review outbound connections from HOST-A2 around the alert time
Disable or reset E2EA\j.doe credentials and review recent logons/privileged actions
Tie this alert to related alert 0104dd4a-2634-48e9-8be1-92c56c9c7380 (ransomware-like renames) into one incident and expand host/user timeline
Collect missing telemetry: process/parent PIDs, integrity level, user SID/logon ID, file hashes, and true source/destination addresses
Confirm whether this is live production activity versus the synthetic E2E marker before irreversible business actions
